handoff.purpose: Defines properties and methods on ShadowResult and the shadow_run function.

symbols.name: ShadowResult.promotion_allowed
symbols.note: Returns bool based on self.discrimination and self.discrimination.proven.

symbols.name: ShadowResult.routed_lane
symbols.note: Returns provider string from attempt.runner_detail dict or None.

symbols.name: ShadowResult.verdict
symbols.note: Returns human-readable verdict string based on state and routed_lane.

symbols.name: ShadowResult.to_dict
symbols.note: Serializes the result to a dict.

symbols.name: shadow_run
symbols.note: Runs one iteration of the circle and returns a ShadowResult.

claims.text: Always False while the gate is unproven. There is no override.
claims.why: Code returns bool(self.discrimination and self.discrimination.proven). If discrimination is None or not proven, returns False. No override mechanism is present.

claims.text: Which provider the router actually chose, read off the runner's own result rather than off the request.
claims.why: Code gets detail from attempt.runner_detail (the runner's result) and extracts 'provider' key.

claims.text: Surfaced because `--local-only` DECLARES availability and does not force the choice: measured, the router still selected `claude_cli` with that lane declared unavailable, and the run stopped only because offload refuses to execute a non-free lane. Nothing was billed, but a run that ends in `no_change` for that reason looks identical to one where the model simply had no idea -- and those are completely different problems.
claims.why: This docstring describes behavior and rationale that cannot be verified from the code in this chunk; it refers to external behavior of the router and offload.

claims.text: One line a human can act on, with the caveat welded to the result.
claims.why: Method returns a string that includes explanation and caveats (e.g., 'This is NOT evidence that the task is hard').

claims.text: ``runner`` is required and has no default, mirroring :class:`daedalus.spine.attempt.TaskAttempt`: no run may quietly reach a model because a caller forgot an argument.
claims.why: shadow_run has a required positional argument 'runner' with no default, and raises ValueError if None or not callable.

claims.text: A receipt proves ONE frozen gate, never 'whatever gate the next candidate happens to use'. Until a candidate exists there is nothing to bind, so the promotion answer is deliberately unproven.
claims.why: Refers to gate_discrimination behavior and reasoning not fully visible in this chunk.

observations.what: promotion_allowed returns False if discrimination is None or not proven; docstring says 'Always False while the gate is unproven' which matches.

routed_lane accesses self.attempt.runner_detail using getattr and checks isinstance(detail, Mapping). If runner_detail is not a dict but has get method, it might still work; but docstring says 'read off the runner's own result' which is consistent.

verdict() method has multiple branches covering no_change, non-gated states, gated but not promotion_allowed, and ready for promotion. It references self.routed_lane which may be None; if None, the string interpolation will include 'None'.
shadow_run function imports build_queue and _head_sha from daedalus.spine.picker inside the function body. This is unusual but not incorrect.
shadow_run calls gate_discrimination with require_gate_binding=True. This function is not defined in this chunk.
